question: 6 women and 4 men can complete a work in 10 days, while 4 women and 5 men complete it in 10 days. In how many days will 8 women complete it?
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Equating efficiencies since the days taken are equal: 6W + 4M = 4W + 5M ⇒ 1M = 2W.

Converting the first group to women: 6W + 4(2W) = 14 Women.

Total work = 14 Women × 10 days = 140 units.

Time for 8 women = 140 ÷ 8 = 17.5 days.

**∴ The correct answer is 17.5 days.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

6 women and 4 men complete the work in 10 days.

4 women and 5 men complete the work in 10 days.

**Formula Used:**

Total Work = Efficiency × Days

**Calculations:**

⇒ 6W + 4M = 1 ... (i)

⇒ 4W + 5M = 1 ... (ii)

⇒ Equating (i) and (ii): 6W + 4M = 4W + 5M

⇒ 5M − 4M = 6W − 4W

⇒ 1M = 2W

⇒ Let the efficiency of 1 woman (W) = 1 unit/day and 1 man (M) = 2 units/day.

⇒ Total work based on the first group = (6 × 1 + 4 × 2) × 10 = (6 + 8) × 10 = 140 units.

⇒ Efficiency of 8 women = 8 × 1 = 8 units/day.

⇒ Time required for 8 women = Total Work ÷ Efficiency of 8 women

⇒ Time required = 140 ÷ 8 = 17.5 days.

**∴ The correct answer is 17.5 days.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Work Equivalence (MDH Rule)

If M₁ persons can do W₁ work in D₁ days, and M₂ persons can do W₂ work in D₂ days, then (M₁ × D₁) ÷ W₁ = (M₂ × D₂) ÷ W₂.

Total Work Concept

Total work is considered constant and is generally found using the LCM of the days taken by different persons or groups.

Efficiency & Time Relation

Efficiency is inversely proportional to time. A person with higher efficiency takes less time to complete the same amount of work.
